html:
SMTO-POL-0021 — This task used up its allowed number of Model decisions

GUID: d82d2877-d3af-451b-9397-1e10255562b8
Slug: model-decision-budget-exhausted
Domain: POL · Subsystem: pol

What happened

  • Each task may ask the Model for only a set number of decisions. This one reached that limit and paused. Its work so far is saved, but it may not have finished checking or describing the result.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the paused task and look at its tool calls and its last message to see what finished. Work done before the pause has already taken effect, even if the task didn't summarize it.
  2. Check the files or items the task was changing to confirm what is actually done. This shows what really changed, so nothing is done twice.
  3. Send a new message asking SMTO to finish only what is left, and name what is already done. A new message starts a task with its own decision allowance, and naming finished work keeps it from being redone.

What success looks like

  • The new task finishes the remaining work and gives a final answer without repeating earlier steps.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. If a small request also hits this limit, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Raising the Model's answer length or timeouts in Settings won't help; this limit counts decisions.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The run's inference budget has no decision slots left (calls reached call_limit, default 128), so the run paused as paused_budget, possibly before the completion step could be finalized.

What this means

  • The inference budget has no remaining decision slot, including a possible unfinished completion-protocol decision after useful work. Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.

Why this can happen

  • The inference budget has no remaining decision slot, including a possible unfinished completion-protocol decision after useful work.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare consumed decisions, retained completion state and operation receipts; distinguish unfinished work from an unfinished completion protocol.

How to fix it

  • Review the run's receipts and completion_recovery state and settle any uncertain operations (llm/budget.py InferenceBudget.consume, native/run_lifecycle.py prepare_turn). Then continue with a new, smaller request or a resume that carries a higher model_limit; output-token or timeout changes don't add decisions, and budget.decision_limit should stay enabled.
  • Review partial progress and retained receipts. Continue through supported task controls only after reconciling unsettled work; increasing output tokens does not increase the decision allowance.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported continuation can make its needed decision within budget while preserving earlier receipts.

What not to do

  • Do not disable the guard as a routine remedy.
  • Do not substitute a different timeout, permission or model setting for this control.

Technical notes

  • Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
